#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euxo pipefail

# =============================================================================
# TypeScript Environment Setup Script - Production Ready
# UnoCSS Repository (preset-wind4.test.ts @ 8da9ff3c6364c8e5abeaaeeaa35400602558127f)
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 1: Configure Environment Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[INFO] Setting TypeScript/Node.js environment variables..."
export NODE_ENV=test
export NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX=/usr/local
export YARN_CACHE_FOLDER=/root/.yarn-cache
export PNPM_STORE_DIR=/root/.pnpm-store
export PATH="/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/root/.local/share/pnpm:$PATH"
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
export LANG=C.UTF-8
export TZ=UTC

# Change to testbed directory (repository already pre-copied & checked out)
cd /testbed
git config --global --add safe.directory /testbed

# Ensure proper permissions for dependency installation
chmod -R 777 /testbed /root/.npm /root/.yarn-cache /root/.pnpm-store /usr/local || true

# Enable Corepack for pnpm
echo "[INFO] Enabling Corepack for pnpm..."
corepack enable
corepack prepare pnpm@latest --activate

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 2: Package Manager Detection & Dependencies Installation
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[INFO] Detecting package manager from lockfiles..."

PACKAGE_MANAGER="npm"
if [ -f "pnpm-lock.yaml" ]; then
    PACKAGE_MANAGER="pnpm"
elif [ -f "yarn.lock" ]; then
    PACKAGE_MANAGER="yarn"
fi
echo "[INFO] Detected package manager: $PACKAGE_MANAGER"

echo "[INFO] Installing dependencies with $PACKAGE_MANAGER..."

case $PACKAGE_MANAGER in
    npm)
        npm ci || echo "WARNING: npm ci failed"
        ;;
    yarn)
        yarn install --frozen-lockfile || echo "WARNING: yarn install failed"
        ;;
    pnpm)
        pnpm install --frozen-lockfile || echo "WARNING: pnpm install failed"
        ;;
esac

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 3: Build & Preparation Commands
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[INFO] Running stub build..."
case $PACKAGE_MANAGER in
    pnpm)
        pnpm stub || echo "WARNING: pnpm stub failed"
        ;;
    yarn)
        yarn stub || echo "WARNING: yarn stub failed"
        ;;
    *)
        npm run stub || echo "WARNING: npm stub failed"
        ;;
esac

echo "[INFO] Running build if available..."
case $PACKAGE_MANAGER in
    pnpm)
        pnpm build || echo "WARNING: pnpm build failed"
        ;;
    yarn)
        yarn build || echo "WARNING: yarn build failed"
        ;;
    *)
        npm run build || echo "WARNING: npm build failed"
        ;;
esac

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 4: TypeScript Compilation Check
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[INFO] Checking TypeScript compilation..."

if [ -f "tsconfig.json" ]; then
    echo "[INFO] Running TypeScript compiler check..."
    pnpm tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json || echo "WARNING: TypeScript compilation check failed"
else
    echo "WARNING: No tsconfig.json found in project root"
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 5: Verification & Output
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[INFO] Environment verification:"
node --version || echo "WARNING: Node.js check failed"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euxo pipefail

# =============================================================================
# TypeScript Environment Setup Script – obsidian-tasks (commit 6e297b90)
# Deterministic, idempotent, production-ready
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 1: Environment Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[INFO] Configuring TypeScript/Node.js environment variables..."
export NODE_ENV=test
export TS_NODE_PROJECT=/testbed/tsconfig.json
export YARN_CACHE_FOLDER=/root/.yarn-cache
export PATH="/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:$PATH"
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
export LANG=C.UTF-8
export TZ=UTC

cd /testbed
git config --global --add safe.directory /testbed
chmod -R 777 /testbed /root/.yarn-cache /usr/local

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 2: Package Manager & Dependencies
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[INFO] Detecting package manager..."
PACKAGE_MANAGER="npm"
if [ -f yarn.lock ]; then
    PACKAGE_MANAGER="yarn"
elif [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ]; then
    PACKAGE_MANAGER="pnpm"
fi
echo "[INFO] Using package manager: $PACKAGE_MANAGER"

echo "[INFO] Installing dependencies (frozen lockfile)..."
case $PACKAGE_MANAGER in
    yarn)
        yarn install --frozen-lockfile --production=false
        ;;
    npm)
        npm ci
        ;;
    pnpm)
        pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
        ;;
esac

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 3: Post-install Build – compile & remove conflicting generated JS mocks
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[INFO] Post-install build: compiling generated JS mocks with TypeScript..."
if [ -f tsconfig.json ]; then
    tsc --project tsconfig.json || echo "[WARN] tsc --project tsconfig.json failed"
fi
# Also run the package's build script if it exists (often triggers same compilation)
case $PACKAGE_MANAGER in
    yarn) yarn build || true ;;
    npm)  npm run build || true ;;
    pnpm) pnpm run build || true ;;
esac

echo "[INFO] Removing duplicate generated JS mocks to avoid Jest conflicts..."
MOCKS_DIR="/testbed/generated/tests/__mocks__"
if [ -d "$MOCKS_DIR" ]; then
    rm -rf "$MOCKS_DIR" || true
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 4: Global Tooling (optional but useful)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[INFO] Installing global TypeScript tooling..."
npm install -g typescript@5.7.2 ts-node@latest || true

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 5: Verification
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[INFO] Environment verification:"
node --version
yarn --version || true
npm --version
tsc --version || true

echo "[INFO] Jest availability:"
npx jest --version || true

echo "[SUCCESS] obsidian-tasks environment ready for testing!"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Completion Marker – DO NOT REMOVE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "=================================="
echo "COMMAND_EXECUTION_COMPLETE"
echo "=================================="

+"""
+Algorithms for computing distance measures on trees.
+"""
+
+import networkx as nx
+from networkx.utils import not_implemented_for
+
+__all__ = [
+    "center",
+]
+
+
+@not_implemented_for("directed")
+def center(G):
+    """Returns the center of an undirected tree graph.
+
+    The center of a tree consists of nodes that minimize the maximum eccentricity.
+    That is, these nodes minimize the maximum distance to all other nodes.
+    This implementation currently only works for unweighted edges.
+
+    If the input graph is not a tree, results are not guaranteed to be correct and while
+    some non-trees will raise an ``nx.NotATree`` exception, not all non-trees will be discovered.
+    Thus, this function should not be used if caller is unsure whether the input graph
+    is a tree. Use ``nx.is_tree(G)`` to check.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    G : NetworkX graph
+        A tree graph (undirected, acyclic graph).
+
+    Returns
+    -------
+    center : list
+        A list of nodes forming the center of the tree. This can be one or two nodes.
+
+    Raises
+    ------
+    NetworkXNotImplemented
+        If the input graph is directed.
+
+    NotATree
+        If the algorithm detects the input graph is not a tree. There is no guarantee
+        this error will always raise if a non-tree is passed.
+
+    Notes
+    -----
+    This algorithm iteratively removes leaves (nodes with degree 1) from the tree until
+    there are only 1 or 2 nodes left. The remaining nodes form the center of the tree.
+
+    This algorithm's time complexity is ``O(N)`` where ``N`` is the number of nodes in the tree.
+
+    Examples
+    --------
+    >>> G = nx.Graph([(1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 4), (2, 5)])
+    >>> nx.tree.center(G)
+    [1, 2]
+
+    >>> G = nx.path_graph(5)
+    >>> nx.tree.center(G)
+    [2]
+    """
+    center_candidates_degree = dict(G.degree)
+    leaves = {node for node, degree in center_candidates_degree.items() if degree == 1}
+
+    # It's better to fail than an infinite loop, so check leaves to ensure progress.
+    while len(center_candidates_degree) > 2 and leaves:
+        new_leaves = set()
+        for leaf in leaves:
+            del center_candidates_degree[leaf]
+            for neighbor in G.neighbors(leaf):
+                if neighbor not in center_candidates_degree:
+                    continue
+                center_candidates_degree[neighbor] -= 1
+                if (cddn := center_candidates_degree[neighbor]) == 1:
+                    new_leaves.add(neighbor)
+                elif cddn == 0 and len(center_candidates_degree) != 1:
+                    raise nx.NotATree("input graph is not a tree")
+        leaves = new_leaves
+
+    n = len(center_candidates_degree)
+    # check disconnected or cyclic
+    if (n == 2 and not leaves) or n not in {1, 2}:
+        # We have detected graph is not a tree. This check does not cover all cases.
+        # For example, `nx.Graph([(0, 0)])` will not raise an error.
+        raise nx.NotATree("input graph is not a tree")
+
+    return list(center_candidates_degree)
